topic: Upper back pain between the shoulder blades

slides.headline: That ache between your shoulder blades
slides.sub: Why it's so common, and simple ways to ease it.

slides.title: Why this spot gets so cranky
slides.body: Long hours at a desk, driving or on your phone keep your upper back in one position. Stress and shallow breathing often add to it. The area can feel tight, achy or burning.

slides.title: Get your upper back rotating
slides.body: Sit tall, cross your arms over your chest and slowly turn side to side. Try 10 turns each way a few times a day. Gentle movement often eases the ache.

slides.title: Open up through the chest
slides.body: Lie on a rolled towel along your spine for a few minutes, or stretch in a doorway. Upper back extension over the back of your chair is another easy option at work.

slides.title: Where chiropractic care fits
slides.body: Hands-on treatment can help your upper back move more comfortably. It tends to work well alongside regular movement, strength work and breaking up long periods of sitting.

slides.title: When to get it checked urgently
slides.body: Upper back pain with chest pain, shortness of breath, sweating or feeling unwell needs urgent medical care. Call 000. Night pain or unexplained weight loss is worth a GP visit.

slides.headline: Upper back feeling locked up?
slides.body: Our chiropractors assess how your upper back and neck move, then combine hands-on care with exercises you can do at your desk.

caption:
That nagging ache between your shoulder blades is one of the most common complaints we hear from desk workers.

Hours in one position, stress and shallow breathing often play a part. Gentle rotation drills, lying on a rolled towel and upper back extension over your chair can help it move more comfortably. Chiropractic care can be a useful add-on alongside regular movement and strength work.

One important note: upper back pain with chest pain, shortness of breath or feeling unwell needs urgent medical care, so call 000.
